name: Tad
label: Sub Pop
lede: Tad Doyle was a butcher from Idaho with a three-song demo. Sub Pop made him a lumberjack, sent him across Europe in a van with Nirvana, and let him make some of the heaviest records out of Seattle.

eras.title: A butcher with a demo
eras.text: Tad Doyle drummed in H-Hour, worked as a butcher, and recorded a demo alone, playing every instrument. Sub Pop's Bruce Pavitt and Jonathan Poneman heard a frontman to build a legend around.

years.h: Sub Pop puts Tad Doyle's name on the band
years.p: Doyle wanted to call it Total Audio Destruction. Pavitt and Poneman insisted on Tad.
years.xp:
Doyle told Vice that the acronym was one of the names he wanted, and that he honestly didn't want the band named after him at first. Sub Pop won, and the name became part of the myth.

The demo had three songs, and Doyle played every instrument on it.

years.h: A bassist, a drummer and a second guitarist make Tad a band
years.p: [[Kurt Danielson|22f1202f-1ab5-41c3-8bc8-bd1d20bbe18b]] (ex-[[Bundle of Hiss|aaa673a8-af81-4140-8cb8-800406c1eace]]) plays bass, Steve Wied (ex-[[Skin Yard|0119843b-4d56-47b6-ac0d-11528259bf0a]]) drums and Gary Thorstensen guitar. Doyle moves to guitar and vocals.

years.h: [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]] produces Tad's first 7-inch, Daisy / Ritual Device
years.p: Sub Pop puts it out in 1988, the year before the first album.

eras.title: A lumberjack myth and a van full of Nirvana
eras.text: Sub Pop sold the band as a butcher and a lumberjack, and the band played along. In late 1989 they crammed into one van with Nirvana for six weeks in Europe; the next record came from Steve Albini.

years.h: God's Balls arrives early in 1989
years.p: Tad's first album comes out on Sub Pop, with Endino producing again.

years.cap: Doyle with a chainsaw and the rest of the band in the woods
q: They liked to kick it up and make it more fantastic than life.
years.h: Sub Pop sells Tad as a butcher and a lumberjack
years.p: Doyle is the Idaho butcher and Danielson comes from a logging town, and the label plays both as backwoods blue-collar types. Doyle says it was all true, just made bigger.
years.xp: Doyle told Vice that Pavitt and Poneman were experts at taking a background and making it bigger than life.

years.h: Tad, Mudhoney and Nirvana play one Lamefest bill at the Moore
years.p: Sub Pop's Lamefest at Seattle's Moore Theatre is the night [[Bruce Pavitt|f5230572-06e4-453c-a1dd-7a4b560da3bb]] later called the turning point for the scene.

yt: 5 facts from Nirvana's 1989 European tour with Tad
years.h: Tad and Nirvana cram into one van to cross Europe
years.p: Heavier Than Heaven starts in Newcastle, both bands in a single small van, mostly sleeping on floors. In Rome, Danielson shouts an insult at the Pope near the Vatican.
years.xp: The tour ran 37 shows in 42 days. [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] got the band thrown out of an Amsterdam hotel, and on the same Rome night, November 27, [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] smashed his guitar and climbed a speaker stack.

years.h: The tour ends at Lamefest UK in London
years.p: Tad play between Nirvana and headliners Mudhoney at the Astoria on Charing Cross Road, Sub Pop's showcase for the British press.

years.h: Albini records Salt Lick, and MTV says no to the video
years.p: The March EP starts as six tracks on vinyl and grows to nine on CD. Wood Goblins gets Tad's first video.
years.xp: MTV rejected the Wood Goblins video, according to Vice, because they thought the band was too ugly for the channel.

eras.title: Sued by Pepsi, sued by a stranger
eras.text: Butch Vig produced Tad's best-known album. Then the cover and a single sleeve brought lawsuits, and Sub Pop changed the art.

years.cap: Doyle singing and playing guitar live, c. 1991
years.h: The Nevermind producer makes 8-Way Santa
years.p: Butch Vig produces Tad's second album, the one with Jinx and Jack Pepsi as singles.

years.h: Pepsi sues over the Jack Pepsi sleeve, and a stranger sues over the cover
years.p: The sleeve swaps the Pepsi logo for Tad's name, and Pepsi objects. Then a woman pictured on the 8-Way Santa cover spots it in Spin and sues too.
years.xp:
The cover was a 1960s thrift-store snapshot of a man fondling a woman's breast. According to Wikipedia, one of the pair had since become a born-again Christian. Sub Pop pulled it and put a band photo on the cover instead.

Doyle told Vice the Pepsi complaint came from a disgruntled former Sub Pop employee, and that the band saw the logo swap as a harmless joke. Both quotes on this card are his, from the same Vice piece.

years.cap: Tad on a Sub Pop press sheet, c. 1991
years.h: Steve Wied quits and Rey Washam sits in on drums
years.p: Wied leaves under the strain of the label and the road. [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]], formerly of [[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]], covers for a short time.
years.xp: Doyle told Vice he might have overstepped his authority with Wied, and that this was one of the reasons, along with being tired of the road, that Wied quit. Wied went on to Willard and Foil.

eras.title: Two majors, two firings
eras.text: A cameo in Cameron Crowe's Singles got Tad a deal with Warner-owned Giant and a record produced by J Mascis. Giant dropped them over a poster the band says it had nothing to do with; East West dropped them two weeks after the next album.

yt: Live at the Seattle Center, July 10, 1992
years.h: Josh Sinder, late of the Accüsed, takes the drum stool
years.p: Sinder debuts on the Salem / Leper single, Tad's last for Sub Pop.

years.h: A Singles cameo leads to a Warner deal at Giant
years.p: After Tad turn up in Cameron Crowe's grunge romance, Giant, a Warner Music label, signs them.

years.h: J Mascis produces Tad's major-label debut, Inhaler
years.p: Recorded at Studio D in Sausalito with [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]]'s Mascis. Reviews are good, sales are not, and the only single is Leafy Incline.

years.big: "And we had nothing to do with that."
years.h: A Bill Clinton poster costs Tad its Giant deal
years.p: Doyle on the Inhaler promo poster that shows Clinton smoking a joint under the line "It's heavy shit". Giant drops the band anyway.
years.xp:
Doyle told Vice the poster came from somebody in the label's art department. It went out on the tour with [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]], and Giant used it as the reason to cut Tad loose.

That tour did little for Tad's sales.

years.h: Futurist Records puts out Live Alien Broadcasts
years.p: A best-of, cut live in the studio, on a small label.

years.h: East West drops Tad two weeks after Infrared Riding Hood
years.p: Gary Thorstensen is gone, so Doyle and Endino play all the guitars. Then the A&R rep who signed Tad is fired, and every band she looked after is dropped.
years.xp: The same rep also looked after [[Clutch|0cdb0359-5698-487d-9aae-a25fb4dcdc4d]]. Doyle told Vice the label barely knew who Tad were by then.

eras.title: Running out of road
eras.text: Tad kept going without a big label, with a new drummer and a few last singles, until the band stopped in 1999.

years.h: Foil's Mike Mongrain replaces Josh Sinder on drums
years.p: Sinder quits to form the Hot Rod Lunatics. Mongrain, who plays in Foil with former Tad drummer Wied, takes the stool.

years.h: Tad's last single is Oppenheimer's Pretty Nightmare
years.p: Seattle's Up Records releases it in 1998, backed with Accident on the Way to Church.

years.h: After eleven years, Tad stops
years.p: The band splits in 1999. Doyle tells Vice that addiction to drugs and alcohol was taking over in the late years, and that he has been sober for years since.
years.xp: "My extracurricular drug activities were becoming paramount instead of the music," Doyle told Vice. "So that started to ruin a lot of things."

eras.title: Heavier, slower, and back in print
eras.text: Doyle went slower and heavier, first in Hog Molly and later in the doom band Brothers of the Sonic Cloth, and ran his own studio. A documentary and a set of Sub Pop reissues put Tad's records back in print.

years.h: Doyle starts Hog Molly with a Willard bassist and a 50 Paces guitarist
years.p: Ty Garcia of Willard and Martin Chandler of 50 Paces join, and the band releases Kung-Fu Cocktail Grip.

yt: TAD: Busted Circuits and Ringing Ears documentary
years.h: A documentary tells the Tad story, lawsuits and all
years.p: Busted Circuits and Ringing Ears has the band and their Seattle peers, including [[Mark Arm|3f99d2df-8859-4249-8a70-84fe04c5a096]], telling it.

years.h: Kurt Danielson comes home from France to write a novel
years.p: Danielson had moved to France after Tad. Back in Seattle, he later plays in Misericords with ex-Tad drummer Mongrain.

years.cap: Doyle playing guitar and singing live in Vancouver
yt: Tad at Sub Pop's 25th Silver Jubilee, July 13, 2013
years.h: Doyle and Thorstensen play Tad songs at Sub Pop's 25th
years.p: At the label's anniversary show they play God's Balls, Salt Lick and 8-Way Santa material, with Brothers of the Sonic Cloth.

years.cap: Doyle (centre) with Brothers of the Sonic Cloth
years.h: Sub Pop reissues the first three Tad albums
years.p: God's Balls, Salt Lick and 8-Way Santa come back in November, remastered by Jack Endino.
years.xp: By then Doyle was in the doom band Brothers of the Sonic Cloth with his wife Peggy and running Witch Ape Studio. He told Vice the band's legacy is its integrity.

years.h: Record Store Day brings out Quick and Dirty
years.p: A vinyl-only release of unreleased Tad songs from 1995 to 1999, plus some live tracks.

sources.title: Vice: Magnets for Ridiculousness: The Story of TAD
Wikipedia: Busted Circuits and Ringing Ears
